title: createViewerAnswer allocates consumers to rejected/inactive SDP offer sections
test: tests/whep.test.js, describe 'createViewerAnswer section eligibility': 'gives the video consumer to the active video section when a disabled (port 0) one comes first'; 'gives the audio consumer to the active audio section when an a=inactive one comes first'; 'answers every section as rejected, with no BUNDLE group, when all sections are disabled or inactive'; 'does not give a consumer to a section the viewer only sends on (sendonly)'; 'omits a=mid from a rejected section when the offer had no mid for it'
proof: Holds. createViewerAnswer looked up consumersByKind[section.kind] for every parsed m-section and deleted the entry on the first match, without looking at the section's port or direction, so a port-0 or a=inactive section ahead of an active one of the same kind took the consumer and was answered with port 9 (and its mid in BUNDLE), while the active section after it fell through to the rejected branch. On the unchanged code, 5 of the 8 new tests failed: the disabled-video-first test with "section should be rejected with port 0: m=video 9 UDP/TLS/RTP/SAVPF 96" (the port-0 section was answered as active), the inactive-audio-first test with the same message for m=audio 9, and the all-disabled test with the same message (every section was active although none was offered). The sendonly test and the no-mid test failed with the same message (a sendonly section and a port-0 section were answered active). Before the fix a rejected section also always printed a made-up a=mid (default '0' or '1', so two rejected video sections shared a mid); the no-mid test pins that, but the port-0 failure came first. The other 3 new tests (no direction attribute counts as sendrecv, an eligible section with no consumer left is rejected in place with its mid, one active section per kind gives an unchanged answer) pass before and after; they guard the behaviour the fix must keep. Fix (lib/whep.js): a new isOfferSectionEligible(section) accepts a section only when port !== 0 and the direction is recvonly or sendrecv (a missing direction is sendrecv, the parser's default); createViewerAnswer gives a consumer only to eligible sections, so the first eligible section of a kind gets it and every other section is answered in place with port 0, a=inactive and its offered a=mid, excluded from a=group:BUNDLE (section-189067a43c5f50160f1b8635/Q-005 default); buildRejectedSection prints a=mid only when the offer had one. The new tests check that the answer has as many m-lines as the offer, in the same order, with the consumer's ssrc and the offered mid on the active section. The 22 existing whep tests, the 10 whepRoutes/session tests and the full suite (508) pass.
